title: required members and MaybeNull / NotNull
hook: required is about definite assignment. MaybeNull and NotNull are about teaching flow analysis a contract the signature cannot spell. Neither is a runtime null shield by itself.

sections.heading: required (C# 11+)
sections.prose: The required modifier on a property or field forces every object initializer (and every constructor that does not opt out) to set that member. Microsoft is explicit: you can still initialize it to null; if the type is a non-nullable reference, that assignment is a warning, not an error. required string AuthorizationHeader { get; init; } is the right shape for an auth options record that must be filled in at construction. required string? OptionalAudience is allowed but usually confused — required means “the caller wrote the property,” not “the value is present.” Types with required members cannot be used as T where T : new() because the compiler cannot run object initializers inside the generic. SetsRequiredMembers on a constructor disables the check; treat that attribute as a loaded gun.

snippets.label: Auth options with required plus attributes
snippets.explanation: required Issuer cannot be omitted. TryReadBearer uses NotNullWhen(true) so callers can use token without ! after a true return.

sections.heading: The analysis attribute set
sections.prose: When T is generic, T? is messy. [return: MaybeNull] on Find<T> says the method may return default even though the return type is T — callers must check. [NotNull] on a parameter says that after the method returns, the argument is not null (ThrowWhenNull). [NotNullWhen(true)] / [NotNullWhen(false)] power Try* and IsNullOrEmpty-style APIs. [NotNullIfNotNull(nameof(input))] says the return is null exactly when input is. [MaybeNullWhen], [DoesNotReturn], [DoesNotReturnIf], [MemberNotNull], and [MemberNotNullWhen] cover helpers that set fields. These live in System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis. They change warnings, not IL. A Redis TryGet that returns bool and sets out T value should use [MaybeNullWhen(false)] so a false result keeps value maybe-null.

sections.heading: Production cache lookup
sections.prose: A generic cache wrapper often wants T? Get<T>(string key). If T is a struct, you just invented Nullable confusion; if T is a class, a miss is null. Prefer TryGet<T>(key, [MaybeNullWhen(false)] out T value) or a Result<T> (module 09). Attributes document the bool; they do not deserialize JSON for you. After a true TryGet, still validate the payload — NRT will not catch a missing nested claim.

interviewTakeaways: required enforces initialization in object initializers; it does not forbid null.
MaybeNull / NotNull / NotNullWhen exist because generic signatures cannot always say T?.
SetsRequiredMembers and null! both turn the compiler off — use them as last resorts.
commonPitfalls: Marking a property required string? and believing the value cannot be omitted and cannot be null.
Returning T from Find without MaybeNull, so callers think a miss is a valid T.
Forgetting [NotNullWhen(true)] on a custom IsPresent, then sprinkling ! at every call site.

jsTsCorrelations.concept: definite assignment and definite assignment assertions
jsTsCorrelations.note: TS definite assignment (!) on fields is cousin to C# required and to field-level !. required is a language error; TS ! is an assertion.
